messages:
alex: Quick follow-up on the paged/blocked KV compatibility with attention kernels — after the RFC there are two open questions I want to resolve before the next rollout: 1) what kernel-side expectations do we keep about contiguous KV vs fragmented pages, and 2) what minimal eviction/pinning API lets runtime do paging without changing kernels.

maria: My take — add a small ABI we call KVView with a few ops: `pin_range(kv_id, start, len) -> ptr|NULL`, `unpin_range(kv_id, start, len)`, `evict_hint(kv_id, ranges[])`, and an advisory `coalesce_hint(kv_id, start, len) -> ranges[]`. Kernels try `pin_range`; if NULL they either yield (if they can) or fall back to CPU-safe path. Runtime handles async prefetch + pin under the hood.

cheng: Two concerns: (a) synchronous `pin_range` in the hot loop can add syscalls/page-fault latency, (b) changing kernels to yield is a large change for most kernels.

jordan: Can we avoid kernel yields? Proposal: `pin_range` returns `NULL` + a short token `async_id`. Kernel checks `if (!ptr) { runtime.prefetch(async_id); goto cpu_fallback }`. That keeps kernel code unchanged except a tiny branch.

maria: Right — that keeps kernel changes minimal. CPU fallback would be slower but bounded. For tail latency we rely on prefetch hints and conservative pinning for hot windows.

alex: Fragmentation is another pain point. If attention windows span many small pages, pin/unpin overhead skyrockets. We should expose a `get_contiguous_ranges(kv_id, start, len)` that attempts to coalesce pages into larger contiguous ranges when possible, and returns the ranges the runtime will actually pin.

cheng: For eviction policy we should keep pinned counters + LRU on unpinned pages. But we also need to track fragmentation ratio per KV: #pages vs #coalesced_ranges. If fragmentation_ratio > threshold, runtime triggers compaction (move data to bigger slabs) or backpressure on writes. Metrics: `page_faults/sec`, `avg_pin_latency_ms`, `fragmentation_ratio`, `pinned_pages_percent`.

jordan: Also important: a tiny fast-path for fully resident KV: `fast_ptr = kvview.peek_range(kv_id, start, len)` which avoids pin bookkeeping when the whole range is resident and the kernel promises not to evict it during use. Use a read-lease model: kernel can call `peek_range` then `confirm_use` so runtime can maintain simple epoch counters instead of per-range locks.

maria: Agree. The lease model reduces contention for common cases. Implementation sketch: `peek_range` returns `ptr` and a `lease_id` if resident; kernel later calls `release_lease(lease_id)`. If not resident, `peek_range` returns NULL and the kernel takes cpu fallback.

prefetch-bot: scheduled prefetch job kv/alpha-3 start=0 len=131072 at 1865432120

cheng: For kernel compatibility we must codify these rules in the ABI doc: what kernels may assume (e.g., `pin_range` never blocks forever; pinned pointers remain valid until `unpin_range`/lease release; `peek_range` is best-effort). Otherwise kernels will make unsafe pointer dereferences.

jordan: Test plan: unit tests for ABI shim, microbench for `pin_range` latency under hit/miss, e2e runs on 2B and 7B models with synthetic long contexts to measure tail latency and token throughput. Also add fault injection that forces eviction mid-request to validate graceful fallback.

alex: Edge-case: checkpoint/rollback interactions. If a migration or checkpoint moves pages, runtime must either block new pins or bump a migration epoch so kernels see `NULL` and fallback. Add `migration_epoch` to ABI so kernel can detect and retry.

maria: Security note: pinned ranges expose memory addresses to kernels. Ensure only sandboxed kernels get direct pointers; untrusted hosted kernels must go through a copy path. Add `pin_caps` with `direct` vs `copy` modes.

alex: Action items: (1) maria: draft ABI doc for KVView + lease semantics (2d), include code examples; (2) cheng: prototype runtime shim + simple compaction heuristic (3d); (3) jordan: bench harness and CPU-fallback microbench (end of week); (4) alex: dashboard metrics names and test matrix. We'll review in arch sync next Tue.

maria: :thumbsup: will start draft.

cheng: I'll spin up a prototype branch and ping for reviews.

jordan: I'll add test cases to perf repo and the fault-injector.

alex: Thanks all — this feels like a pragmatic path to keep kernels unchanged while enabling paging.
